create_image.summary: Create a new image from a description, or modify an image.
create_image.guidance: Use only when the user asks for an image to be produced or changed; writing or improving a prompt alone does not mean generating. The image model only sees the images passed in source and reference: an image that is only described in the prompt is not used.
create_image.prompt: The whole image, written for an image model that knows nothing of this conversation: three to six sentences in English. Say the subject with its concrete look (age, expression, pose, clothes, colours, materials), the place and what is behind, the framing (how close, from which angle, what is in the foreground), the light and the colours, and the kind of picture (photo with its lens and film look, illustration, painting, 3D render). Text to write in the image goes in quotes, in the language asked. Only concrete, visible things: a word like "beautiful" or "high quality" alone says nothing. Keep everything the user asked for.

source.description: Image to modify. Omit to create a new image.

reference.description: Images whose subject, character or style must be reused.

create_video.summary: Create a video clip from a description, optionally starting or ending on given images or keeping a subject from reference images.
create_video.guidance: Propose a video only when the user asks for one. Every video is shown to the user, who can edit it before it runs. The video model only sees the images passed in start_image, end_image and reference: an image that is only described in the prompt is not used. When the request involves several images, pass every one of them, each in the role that fits. Before generating, agree on the video with the user in one short spoken message, without a tool: five lines at most, plain sentences, no headings, no lists, no bold. Say how you understand the clip, the length in seconds, what each image is for, then ask one to three questions only about what is still open or could be read two ways, and ask for their go. Do not write the full prompt there. Call this tool once they answered.
create_video.prompt: The whole clip, written for a video model that knows nothing of this conversation: one paragraph of five to eight sentences in English, present tense, in the order things happen. Say what is seen (who or what, with their look: age, hair, clothes, colours, materials; the place, the time of day, the light), then what happens beat by beat with the gestures and their pace, then how the camera moves (from where to where, how fast, how it ends), the look of the picture (live action, animation, film grain, lens), and the sound, since the clip has sound: ambience, noises, and any spoken words in quotes, in the language they are spoken. With a start image, still describe in a sentence what that image shows, then put the detail on what moves, what changes and where the camera goes. Only concrete, visible or audible things: a word like "cinematic" or "smooth" alone says nothing. Keep everything the user asked for, in their order. Naming an image here does not show it to the video model.

start_image.description: Image the video starts on, as its first frame: the choice to animate an image or to make a video from it.

end_image.description: Image the clip must end on exactly, as its last frame. Only when the user asks for that in so many words (an end image, a last frame, "finit sur cette image"). A place, an object or a person the camera goes to, reveals or discovers during the clip is not an end image: pass it in reference.

reference.description: Images of a person, a character, an object or a place that must appear in the clip, kept as they look: also what the camera goes to or reveals during the clip (the camera then turns to a door: the image of that door is a reference). They are not frames of the clip: to animate an image, use start_image. Between end_image and reference, choose reference unless the user asked for an exact last frame.

extend_video.summary: Continue an existing video with a new shot that follows its last frames.
extend_video.guidance: Every video is shown to the user, who can edit it before it runs. Before generating, agree with the user in one short spoken message, without a tool (five lines at most, plain sentences, no lists), on what happens next and for how many seconds; call this tool once they answered.
extend_video.prompt: What happens next, written for a video model that only sees the last frames of the source: three to six sentences in English, present tense. Say who or what is on screen in a few words, then the new action beat by beat, how the camera moves and ends, and the sound (ambience, noises, spoken words in quotes, in the language they are spoken). Only concrete, visible or audible things.

reference.description: Images of a person, a character, an object or a place that must appear in the continuation, kept as they look: someone who enters the shot, or what the camera turns to. Not frames of the clip.

create_audio.summary: Create music (a song with sung lyrics, or an instrumental piece) or sound effects from a description.
create_audio.guidance: Use only when the user asks for music or a sound to be produced; writing lyrics alone does not mean generating. Every sound is shown to the user, who can edit it before it runs. You cannot hear the result: to judge it, ask the user. For a song, write the lyrics in full yourself unless the user gave them, and pass them in lyrics.
create_audio.prompt: The sound, written for an audio model that knows nothing of this conversation, in English. For music: a comma-separated list of tags, then one sentence: genre and era, mood, tempo in BPM, key if it matters, the instruments, the voice (female or male, its tone, sung or rapped) or "instrumental", and the production (lo-fi, live room, polished studio). For a sound effect: one or two sentences saying what makes the sound, the material, the action and its rhythm, the place and its acoustics (small room, open field, street), how near it is, and what comes before or after. Only concrete, audible things: a word like "epic" or "beautiful" alone says little. Never put the lyrics here.

upscale.summary: Increase the resolution and sharpness of an existing image or video.
upscale.guidance: Use when the user wants a larger or sharper version of an existing result.

interpolate.summary: Make an existing video smoother by adding intermediate frames.
interpolate.guidance: Use when the user wants a smoother or slow-motion version of an existing video.
